surprises.description: The preview looked for organic growth of about 4.5% in H2, but Q3 organic growth was 4%. The tornado explains roughly 1 percentage point of growth: excluding it, organic growth was 5%, while business-interruption insurance offset the lost operating income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 organic growth was 4% (5% excluding the tornado event)” and the tornado “reduced Q3 revenue by about $40 million (roughly 1 percentage point of growth), with the lost operating income offset by business interruption insurance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management framed H2 organic at ~4.5% (Q2's pace)” and the checklist called for “Organic growth ≥4.5%.”

surprises.description: Automotive OEM organic revenue fell 2%, rather than returning to the positive growth the preview expected. Its margin also fell 170 basis points amid resin inflation and price/cost timing lag, although ITW outperformed build rates in North America and China.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Automotive OEM organic revenue fell 2% with operating margin down 170 basis points due to resin inflation and price/cost timing lag,” while the company “outperformed build rates in North America and China.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The segment consensus was “+0.5%” organic, and the preview said Auto OEM was a low-expectation inflection to watch, with management’s guide to outgrow builds.

surprises.description: Test & Measurement and Electronics delivered 16% organic growth, well above the preview’s roughly 10.5% segment revenue-growth estimate; electronics alone grew 31%. Segment margin expanded 330 basis points to 28.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Test & Measurement and Electronics delivered 16% organic growth led by a 31% surge in electronics, with operating margin expanding 330 basis points to 28.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Test & Measurement / Electronics consensus revenue growth of “+10.5%” and described it as an “AI infra / semi capex engine.”

surprises.description: Construction Products declined 1% organically instead of growing around the preview’s 1.4% revenue estimate, and its margin fell 170 basis points on price/cost headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Construction Products organic revenue declined 1% with margin down 170 basis points on price/cost headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Construction Products revenue growth of “+1.4%” and described the segment as “Housing-constrained.”

surprises.description: Within Construction Products, commercial construction surged 19% on data-center demand, an unexpectedly strong pocket of growth despite the segment’s overall decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial construction (15% of the region) surged 19% on data center demand.”

surprises.description: Management said customer-back innovation is contributing more than 3% to revenue growth and raised the full-year projection to 3%-plus. The preview did not flag this growth contribution or a higher projection as an expectation to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer-back innovation (CBI) is contributing more than 3% to revenue growth versus 2.4% in 2025, and the full-year CBI projection was raised to 3%-plus.”

surprises.description: Management put a specific best-in-class margin range on Welding’s recovery, saying margins are expected to return to 32%-34% as orders run well ahead of revenue. The preview expected orders to outpace revenue but did not anticipate this margin-range outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Welding “is expected to return to best-in-class margins of 32%-34% as order growth runs well ahead of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether “order growth” continued to “outpace revenue growth” in Welding, but gave no Welding margin-recovery range.
